area: V2X radio / communication model (message delivery, channel, losses, latency)
current_state:
TWO independent radio implementations exist.

== A. Pure-Python mock pipeline (src/scms_sim_ref/mock_pipeline/run.py, 3436 lines) — the primary dataset engine ==

CONFIG (PipelineConfig, run.py:337-363; validation run.py:911-926; CLI run.py:3172-3187; GUI help run.py:1306-1328): radio_range_m=500 (hard reception range), packet_loss_base=0.0, nlos_loss=0.0, chan_capacity=40 (in-range CAMs/step before congestion loss), radio_model="disc"|"logdistance" (default "disc"), pathloss_exponent=2.7, shadowing_sigma_db=4.0, rx_sensitivity_margin_db=0.0, radio_cap_sigma=4.0 / radio_cap_max_mult=6.0 (run.py:256-261 module constants), art_max_m=150 (acceptance-range detector tolerance), rsu_range_m (run.py:490, 0 = use radio_range_m; applied to RSU receivers run.py:1812,1821), net_delay_max=2.0 s and crl_propagation_delay=2.0 s (run.py:334-335). Weather tables at run.py:137-139: WEATHER_RADIO_LOSS = clear 0.0, rain 0.03, fog 0.02, snow 0.06 (flat extra Bernoulli drop probability); weather can change mid-run via the events timeline (run.py:765, 805-808, weather_at() run.py:1479-1487).

BEACONING: every active, non-revoked, non-jammed vehicle emits exactly ONE CAM per step (fixed 1 Hz at default dt=1.0, run.py:274) in the broadcast pre-pass (run.py:2544-2650). DoS attackers set msg_count=dos_burst=12 (run.py:2578-2587) but only one content instance exists — msg_count only inflates the receiver's load counter (run.py:2746) and the beaconFrequency detector (run.py:2825). No ETSI EN 302 637-2 CAM generation rules (dynamics-triggered 1-10 Hz) in this layer. Sybil ghosts are extra broadcast dicts at the attacker's position (run.py:2641-2650). Opt-in DENMs are extra broadcasts (run.py:2118-2147). VRUs transmit but never receive (run.py:2682); RSUs receive but never transmit (run.py:1807-1826).

DELIVERY (receiver-outer detection pass, run.py:2673-2752): spatial hash with cell = radio_range (run.py:2689-2696); per-receiver range rr = rx.rx_range or cfg.radio_range_m (run.py:2704).
1. Link closure, two modes:
   - "disc" (DEFAULT): heard iff Euclidean distance d <= rr — a hard unit-disk cutoff (run.py:2728-2730). Byte-identical golden-digest contract (tests/test_radio_propagation.py:20,75-80).
   - "logdistance" (OPT-IN): mean received power relative to sensitivity mean_db = 10*n*log10(rr/max(d,1)) - rx_sensitivity_margin_db (0 dB exactly at d==rr, so median range == radio_range_m; run.py:2738-2739) plus per-link log-normal shadow ~ N(0, shadowing_sigma_db) drawn from a DEDICATED string-keyed RNG random.Random(f"{seed}:shadow:{tx_cert_digest}:{rx.vid}:{step}") (run.py:2742-2743); heard iff mean_db + shadow_db >= 0 (run.py:2744). Candidate window widened to cap = rr * 10^((cap_sigma*sigma - min(0,margin))/(10n)), clamped to rr*cap_max_mult (run.py:2709-2712).
2. Per-packet drop on closed links (run.py:2746-2752): loss = packet_loss_base + nlos_loss*(dist/rr) + cong + wx_loss, single uniform draw from the GLOBAL rng (run.py:2751). cong = min(0.8, max(0,(load - chan_capacity)/chan_capacity)*0.5) where load = sum of msg_count over this receiver's in-range broadcasts this step (run.py:2746-2747) — a per-receiver CBR proxy. NLOS is a pure linear-in-distance ramp, not geometry-based.
3. LATENCY: none at the radio layer. Reception is same-step and instantaneous; MaReport detection_time == generation_time == t (run.py:2082). The only delays modeled: report ingest delay = rng.uniform(0, net_delay_max) applied to ingest_time (run.py:2079-2082), and CRL enforcement lag crl_propagation_delay (run.py:2176-2177). Message-timing attacks are modeled purely via the CLAIMED gen-time cg (DelayedMessages/DataReplay/OutOfOrder, run.py:2580-2585) feeding the staleOrReplay detector (run.py:2826).
4. Radio-coupled detectors: acceptanceRangeThreshold = max(0, d(rx,claimed) - rr)/art_max_m using the actual per-receiver rr (run.py:2818-2824); beaconFrequency = msg_count/freq_max (run.py:2825).

== B. MOSAIC/SUMO layer (scms-sim/) ==
Network federate is MOSAIC SNS only — omnetpp/ns3/cell federates are explicitly False (scms-sim/scenarios/mapgen.py:399-400; scms-sim/scenarios/scms_smoke/scenario_config.json federates block). SNS config generated by mapgen.write_sns_config (mapgen.py:159-172; instance at scms-sim/scenarios/gen_smoke/sns/sns_config.json): maximumTtl 10, singlehopRadius = env SCMS_RADIO_RANGE default 709.4 m, adhocTransmissionModel "SophisticatedAdhocTransmissionModel", singlehopDelay SimpleRandomDelay 5 steps 0.4-2.4 ms, singleHopTransmission lossProbability = env SCMS_RADIO_LOSS default 0.0, maxRetries 0. NOTE: the scms_smoke scenario directory has NO sns/ folder at all (only application/mapping/output/sumo) despite "sns": true in its scenario_config.json.
App layer (scms-sim/mosaic-apps/scms-app/src/main/java/org/scms/app/ScmsBeaconApp.java): AdHoc module enabled with a single CCH radio, power(50) (lines 120-121); topological singlehop broadcast (lines 192-196). ETSI CAM generation rules ARE implemented here: T_GenCamMin 0.1 s / T_GenCamMax 1.0 s, triggers dPos>4 m / dHdg>4 deg / dSpd>0.5 m/s (lines 40-41, 140-155). Receiver-side stacked Bernoulli drops in onMessageReceived, using a deterministic per-vehicle RNG (line 119): weather drop rain 0.05 / fog 0.03 / snow 0.10 (lines 54-66, 210-213); NLOS ramp p = SCMS_NLOS * clamp((dist-150)/300, 0, 1) with dist computed from cam.claimedX/Y — the CLAIMED, attacker-controlled position, not the true sender position (lines 55, 214-221); congestion: 0.1 s sliding window, CHAN_CAPACITY default 25 CAMs/100 ms, pDrop = min(0.95, (load-cap)/cap) (lines 52-53, 109-111, 226-235).

== C. Per-message schema (src/scms_sim_ref/schemas/records.py) ==
MaEvidenceMessage (records.py:71-87): msg_ref, subject_cert_digest, gen_time, claimed_x/y/speed/heading, sig_valid, cert_status_at_eval — NO rssi, NO snr, NO rx position, NO rx timestamp, NO per-message delay. MaReport (records.py:90-109): ingest_time / detection_time / generation_time (detection==generation always), st_bbox, reason_codes, detector_outputs. Ad-hoc row extras added at run.py:2091-2099 (detector_score, detnorm_*, subject_pos_confidence) — no radio measurement of any kind. FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_KEYS leakage registry (records.py:33-65) would gate any new true-value radio field.

Tests pinning behavior: tests/test_radio.py (range limits report graph, packet loss reduces reports, DoS/Delayed trigger detectors), tests/test_radio_propagation.py (disc golden digest, soft-range beyond rr under logdistance, sigma=0 collapse to disc, determinism, exponent monotonicity).
gaps: No small-scale fading anywhere: even the opt-in logdistance model is path-loss + log-normal shadowing only; real 5.9 GHz V2V PDR at mid-range is dominated by Rayleigh/Rician/Nakagami-m fading (Nakagami m~3 near, m~1 far is the standard VANET model). Default 'disc' is a pure unit-disk.

Shadowing has zero temporal/spatial correlation: the shadow draw is keyed f'{seed}:shadow:{cert_digest}:{rx.vid}:{step}' (run.py:2742-2743), i.i.d. per step, so links flicker at 1 Hz instead of persisting over seconds (real shadowing has a Gudmundson decorrelation distance ~10-50 m); worse, keying on the CERT digest means a pseudonym rotation resamples the propagation environment.

No building/obstacle-geometry NLOS: nlos_loss is a linear distance ramp (run.py:2750) and the Java NLOS ramp starts at a hardcoded 150 m (ScmsBeaconApp.java:217); the OSM importer (osm.py:94-104) pulls only highway=* ways — no building footprints — so no geometric LOS test (e.g., Boban vehicles-as-obstacles or ns-3 obstacle shadowing) is possible today, even for real-city maps.

No MAC layer at all: no CSMA/CA contention, no hidden-terminal collisions, no EDCA queues, no capture effect, no half-duplex (a transmitting vehicle still receives everything). 'Congestion' is a receiver-side heuristic Bernoulli ramp (mock: slope 0.5 capped 0.8, run.py:2747; Java: min(0.95,(load-cap)/cap), ScmsBeaconApp.java:230-234), not slot-level contention; a DoS flood only inflates a load counter — every surviving frame still delivers with zero delay.

No CBR measurement or DCC: no channel-busy-ratio observable, no ETSI TS 102 687 DCC (reactive/adaptive CAM-rate throttling), so honest vehicles never reduce beacon rate under load; chan_capacity thresholds (40/step mock, 25/100 ms Java) are arbitrary and unconnected to any PHY data-rate/airtime budget.

No per-packet latency or jitter in the mock pipeline: delivery is same-step instantaneous (detection_time==generation_time, run.py:2082); the MOSAIC SNS layer has only a uniform 0.4-2.4 ms random delay (mapgen.py:166-167). No queuing, no retransmission, no distance-dependent or load-dependent latency.

No radio-technology model: no DSRC/ITS-G5 802.11p vs C-V2X (LTE-V2X PC5 mode 4 SPS, NR-V2X) distinction, no data rate/MCS, no frame airtime, no SPS persistent-collision behavior; single channel (CCH) only, no multi-channel/SCH, no channel switching.

RSSI/SNR are never computed, logged, or exposed: MaEvidenceMessage (records.py:71-87) carries no signal-strength field, so the entire RSSI-vs-claimed-distance misbehavior-detector family (standard in F2MD/VeReMi-style datasets — VeReMi itself ships per-message RSSI) cannot be reproduced, and ML features have no PHY-layer plausibility signal. Sybil ghosts consequently have no shared-radio PHY signature (identical RSSI/DoA) despite physically sharing one transmitter (run.py:2641-2650).

Loss composition is additive, not independent-survival: loss = base + nlos*(d/rr) + cong + wx can exceed 1.0 and double-counts mechanisms (run.py:2750); draws come from the single GLOBAL rng stream (run.py:2751), coupling radio outcomes to every other stochastic subsystem's draw order.

No transmitter heterogeneity: all vehicles share one implicit power/antenna (only RSU rx range differs, run.py:1812); no per-vehicle TX power, antenna height/gain, truck-vs-car antenna height, vehicle-body attenuation, or lower-power VRU smartphone radios (VRUs transmit with full vehicle range).

Weather radio effect is a flat heuristic Bernoulli drop (rain 0.03/fog 0.02/snow 0.06, run.py:138; rain 0.05/fog 0.03/snow 0.10 in Java, ScmsBeaconApp.java:60-64) rather than a physical dB attenuation (real rain attenuation at 5.9 GHz is <0.01 dB/km — the two layers even disagree with each other).

MOSAIC-layer specific: SNS SophisticatedAdhocTransmissionModel is still a radius+delay abstraction (no PHY); the app-layer NLOS drop uses the attacker-CONTROLLED claimed position (ScmsBeaconApp.java:216) so a position-falsifying attacker perturbs its own link loss; the scms_smoke scenario is missing its sns/ config directory entirely while declaring the sns federate enabled; omnetpp/ns3 federate flags exist but are hardwired False (mapgen.py:400).
No multi-hop/geo-networking: singlehop broadcast only in both layers (fine for CAM, but DENM repetition/geobroadcast forwarding is absent), maxRetries=0, no store-and-forward via RSUs.

Mock-pipeline beaconing is a fixed 1 CAM/step (1 Hz) with no ETSI dynamics-triggered generation (that exists only in the Java layer, ScmsBeaconApp.java:140-155), so beacon-rate realism and rate-based congestion feedback are absent from the layer that actually produces the datasets.
opportunities: Single choke point for a proper channel model: the reception loop run.py:2697-2752. The link-closure branch (run.py:2728-2745) is where fading plugs in (e.g., add a Nakagami-m per-packet fade to mean_db+shadow_db before the >=0 test); the per-packet loss line (run.py:2750-2752) is where composition should become an independent-survival product p_deliver = (1-p_base)*(1-p_nlos)*(1-p_cong)*(1-p_wx).

The repo's established, digest-safe extension pattern is ready to reuse: opt-in config knob defaulting to legacy behavior + a DEDICATED string-keyed RNG stream (random.Random(f'{seed}:name:...'), e.g. run.py:2742, 1801-1805) so the default stays byte-identical to the golden digest (tests/test_radio_propagation.py:20). Any new channel feature (fading, correlated shadowing, CBR/DCC, latency) must follow it.

Correlated shadowing fix is cheap: key the shadow on the TRUE vehicle id (b['veh'].vid) instead of cert digest, and evolve it as an OU process across steps (state kept per (tx_vid, rx_vid) alongside last_claimed) instead of resampling per step — gives Gudmundson-style temporal correlation with no new architecture.

Per-receiver channel load is ALREADY computed (load, run.py:2746) — derive a real CBR observable (load * frame_airtime / dt), log it, and gate a DCC model in the broadcast pre-pass (run.py:2544-2650), which is also the hook point to port the Java layer's ETSI CAM generation rules (ScmsBeaconApp.java:140-155) into the Python engine (dynamics-triggered 1-10 Hz beaconing).

RSSI observable is one line once logdistance is on: rx position and distance are in hand at detection time (run.py:2727, 2823), and mean_db+shadow_db is the received power relative to sensitivity — attach it to the broadcast/report row (row assembly run.py:2081-2099) and to MaEvidenceMessage (records.py:71-87), enabling the RSSI-vs-claimed-distance detector family and PHY-consistent Sybil ghosts (ghosts inherit the attacker's true-position RSSI). Gate new fields through FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_KEYS (records.py:33-65).

Per-packet latency: add a delivery-delay model (propagation + MAC queuing as f(load)) and buffer broadcasts across steps (broadcasts list, run.py:2545, currently consumed same-step); detection_time vs generation_time in MaReport (records.py:94-95) already has the schema slots to express it.

Building-aware NLOS: extend osm.py (way parsing at osm.py:94-104) to also pull building=* footprints from the same Overpass/XML source, store them beside the custom-network JSON, and replace the linear nlos_loss ramp with a segment-intersection LOS test (spatial-hash the footprints like the broadcast cells at run.py:2689-2696); fall back to per-edge 'urban canyon' density on synthetic grids (roads.py already knows the graph).

Technology profiles: a radio_profile knob ('dsrc-11p' | 'cv2x-mode4') selecting parameter bundles (range, fading m, MAC-loss curve, latency distribution, SPS-collision term) would give the C-V2X/DSRC distinction without a full PHY; validation + FIELD_HELP + GROUPS registries (run.py:911-926, 1101-1114, 1306-1328) make new knobs self-describing in the GUI (gui/server.py:473-476).

MOSAIC layer upgrades: the federate flags for omnetpp/ns3 already exist (mapgen.py:399-400) — wiring the MOSAIC OMNeT++ ambassador (toolchain at C:/Users/Administrator/tools, MOSAIC 25.2) would buy a real 802.11p PHY/MAC wholesale; short of that, fix the claimed-position NLOS bug (ScmsBeaconApp.java:216 — get true sender distance from the ScmsBackend oracle), unify the two layers' divergent weather-loss tables (run.py:138 vs ScmsBeaconApp.java:60-64), and generate the missing sns/ dir for scms_smoke.

The events timeline (run.py:765, 805-808) already supports mid-run weather fronts that change wx_loss — a natural hook for RF-jamming events, channel outages, or interference zones as new event types (attack_wave/zone machinery at run.py:2555-2556 shows the geographic-gating pattern).

Jamming/interference as an attack class: gps_jam_rate models GNSS outage (run.py:305-306, 2568-2573) but RF jamming of the V2X channel itself (zone-based elevated loss) is absent and would slot into the same reception loop with an event-driven loss term.
notes: Hard project invariant discovered: the DEFAULT config must stay byte-identical (golden digest DEFAULT_GOLDEN pinned at tests/test_radio_propagation.py:20; every radio feature to date — logdistance, RSUs, VRUs, DENMs — was added as opt-in with dedicated keyed RNG streams precisely to preserve it). Any state-of-the-art channel model MUST be introduced the same way (new radio_model value or opt-in knobs), or the whole determinism test suite breaks. Key line anchors for the delivery pipeline: weather tables run.py:137-139; radio config block run.py:337-363; reception loop run.py:2673-2752 (disc cutoff 2728-2730, logdistance closure 2732-2745, congestion 2746-2747, composed per-packet loss 2750-2752); report ingest delay run.py:2079; CRL lag run.py:2177; ART detector run.py:2818-2824. Java layer: SNS radius/delay/loss mapgen.py:159-172; app-layer weather/NLOS/congestion drops ScmsBeaconApp.java:52-66 and 209-235 (NLOS uses claimed position — line 216, a realism bug). Per-message schema has no RSSI/SNR/delay fields (records.py:71-109). The two layers' loss models are independently implemented and numerically inconsistent (e.g., rain drop 0.03 vs 0.05; chan capacity 40/step vs 25/100ms).
